anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet (mcu.kicad_sch, page 1/4, top-right), the USB-C receptacle J6 VBUS pin (A4) is tied to the VBUS global label (the power-mux output net that feeds the buck) at the same node as the +5V power symbol, instead of being routed to the +5V net that drives U9 (TPS2121RUXR) IN2 (pin 2).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the USB VBUS pins go to the +5V net which feeds U9 IN2, and explicitly notes that the mux output net 'VBUS' is 'distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.' The USB VBUS pin must connect to +5V only, never to VBUS.

evidence.quote: J12 (USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_14P) VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) → +5V net → U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2).
outputs a single OUT ... onto the VBUS net (the board's internal, unregulated/pre-buck rail — note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux).
mcu.kicad_sch page 1/4, J6 USB_C_Receptacle: pin A4 carries the VBUS global label at the same node as the +5V power arrow.

anomalies.impact: The +5V input net and the arbitrated VBUS output net are merged. When powered from the 12 V barrel jack the mux output (~12 V) is driven onto the USB connector's VBUS pin, back-powering/over-volting the host port, while U9 IN2 (+5V) is never powered from USB, so USB-only operation fails. The two rails the spec requires to be separate are shorted together.
